# Overflow control on an unfocused pane needs two clicks to open its menu

## Context

Found by the gate-3 non-author walk of `apps/workstation` on the v13.3.1 candidate `e2f77dd0fb` (receipt on #20022, finding 2). Ordinary pointer input in headed Chrome, 1440×900, standalone Workstation. First recorded as a design note; promoted to a milestone ticket by the operator's ruling of 2026-10-23 (~14:00 CEST): the version handed to the external tester carries no known bug.

## The Problem

The `Priority Alert Observatory` strip holds more tabs than fit, so it shows the overflow control (`…`, title "More tabs"). With the pane **unfocused**, one click on that control:

1. focuses the pane — the focus-gated action rail (pin, reload, pop out, maximize, close) renders in the strip;
2. the strip re-partitions for the rail's width — `Resident Activity Timeline` moves into overflow and the control itself moves ≈ 100 px to the left, out from under the pointer;
3. **no menu opens** (checked at 250 ms and 1.1 s after the click; no element with a menu/overflow class was visible).

A second click on the control at its new position opens the menu with the hidden tabs. Observed 2/2 in the walk (sessions a: gestures 06 and 09/10). A user sees their click do something unrelated (the pane highlights, a tab vanishes into overflow) and the affordance they clicked slide away.

## The Architectural Reality (inference, to be verified by the owner)

- The header action rail is focus-gated (#17875 lineage; #19983 added the hover-reveal option, off by default here), so the first pointer-down on anything in an unfocused strip focuses the pane and the rail appears in the same strip.
- The tab overflow plugin partitions on the strip's free width; the rail takes ~120 px, so the partition changes under the pointer and the control is re-laid out. #20033 / #20039 settled the e2e oracle for the partition at menu open; they did not touch the first-click behaviour.
- The click that focused the pane does not reach the overflow control's open handler (either the control is re-rendered before `click` lands, or focus handling consumes it).

## The Fix (prescription, owner's call)

One click opens the menu, focused or not. Two shapes, both acceptable:

- open the menu from the same click after the re-partition settles (anchor the menu to the control's new position); or
- reserve the rail's width in the strip's partition (or anchor the overflow control at the strip's right edge independent of the rail), so nothing moves under the pointer and the click lands on the control it was aimed at.

Keep the focused-strip behaviour unchanged (one click opens today).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: red-first e2e arm (pointer click on the overflow control of an **unfocused** strip): the menu is open within the settle window after one click on `e2f77dd0fb` → red; green at head.
- [ ] AC-2: after that click the control's rect either did not move or the menu is anchored to its new rect — no second click needed.
- [ ] AC-3: the focused-strip arm (one click opens) stays green; `WorkstationMaximizeOverflowMenuNL` and #20039's arm stay green.
- [ ] AC-4 (post-merge): one full local `e2e/workstation` + `e2e/dashboard` run green.

## Out of Scope

The hover-reveal option (#19983) itself; the overflow partition oracle (#20033); #20045.

## Related

#20022 (cut record; walk receipt) · #19983 (hover reveal of focus-gated actions) · #20033 / #20039 (overflow-menu spec) · #17875 (focus-gated actions) · D#19994 (walk charter).

## Shipped shape (PR #20052)

A third shape, not one of the two above: the toolbar can hold a focus-gated reveal for a named reason, and the overflow plugin holds it for exactly as long as a press can still click the control, then hands it to the menu the click opens for as long as that menu is mounted, so nothing in the strip moves until the user is done with the menu; the owed reveal lands when the menu closes. No timer decides when a press ends (the review's RA-1 removed a 1500 ms safety timer and a 250 ms post-click delay from the first head). Two other shapes were built, measured and withdrawn: reserving the rail's span in the partition (a 180 px single-tab strip truncated its only tab, a 220 px two-tab strip hid a tab that fit) and placing the contribution after the focus-gated actions (it contradicted the toolbar's documented contract and the frozen rail order a spec pins; the hold made it unnecessary). AC-1/AC-2 are the e2e arms (the 120 ms press red on e2f77dd0fb, the 2 s press red on the first head, both green at head); AC-3 the overflow/header-action specs; AC-4 the full local battery, receipt on the PR.

## Contract Ledger (the consumed hold contract, PR #20052 · review RA-2)

| Surface | Status | Semantics | Acquire / release ownership | Controls |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `toolbar.Base#holdContextualReveal(reason)` | internal owner/plugin seam (`@protected`), no public-API obligation | adds `reason` to `contextualRevealHolds` (a Set): idempotent per reason, a repeated hold with the same reason is one entry; while any reason is held, a focus-gated reveal (`showOnFocus` actions whose context turns active) stays withdrawn and `contextualRevealPending` is set; a hold never withdraws an already revealed action; the hidden measurement reveal (`measuringContextualActions`) ignores holds | the plugin that needs the strip still acquires; the toolbar's `destroy` nulls the Set | unit `HeaderActions.spec` "a held reveal keeps withdrawn actions withdrawn until the last release, never withdraws a revealed one, and a keyboard-only focus is unaffected" |
| `toolbar.Base#releaseContextualReveal(reason)` | same | deletes `reason`; releasing a reason that is not held is a no-op; the last release with a pending reveal applies `applyContextualActionState()` once | the acquiring plugin releases every reason it took, at the latest in its `destroy` | the same unit arm (the owed reveal lands on the last release) |
| `tab.plugin.Overflow` reason `'overflow-control'` | internal | taken by a primary press (`mousedown`, `button === 0`) on the control; released at the first of: the menu list's `mounted` flipping true after a click that opens the menu (`'overflow-menu'` is taken first, so there is no gap), a click that closes the menu or opens none, `mouseleave` during the press (taken again on `mouseenter` with the primary button still down; a return with the button up ends the press), the action-mode teardown when every tab fits (the control hides under the pointer), the plugin's `destroy` — never a clock | the plugin | unit `Overflow.spec` "a press holds the reveal while it can still click the control, and no clock ends it" and "a click that opens the menu hands the hold to it at its mount without a gap; a click that closes it releases at once"; e2e `WorkstationMaximizeOverflowMenuNL`: the 120 ms press and the 2 s press on an unfocused pane |
| `tab.plugin.Overflow` reason `'overflow-menu'` | internal | taken when the generated menu list's `mounted` flips true (the click that opens the menu observes the list itself once `menuListReady` settles), released when it flips false (the owed reveal lands then) and in `destroy` | the plugin | e2e: the docked and maximized menu arms (the rail lands after Escape) |
| measurement reveal (`toolbar.Base#setContextualActionMeasureReveal`) | internal | probes with `measuringContextualActions = true`, outside the hold; the restore writes `visibility: null` (a deleted key never leaves a merged vdom style) and lands before the withdraw | toolbar | e2e `WorkstationHeaderActionsHoverNL` (hover mode's probe path) |

Residual edges, bounded and never under an active press: a press abandoned over the control (the button released off-page) keeps the hold until the pointer leaves the control; a hide and re-show of the menu that coalesce without a `mounted` flip keep it until the next closing click or the control's teardown.
